text.p: A Polish parliamentarian who observed a self-styled referendum staged by Italy's Northern League said he wanted to learn more about separatist trends, PAP news agency reported on Monday.

Jerzy Pistelok, an MP of the co-ruling Polish Peasant Party (PSL), told PAP he had attended the exercise on Sunday out of "curiosity and a need to become better orientated on how separatist tendencies look in Western Europe."

Pistelok explained he wanted to know why North Italians were seeking to set up the independent state of Padania and compared it to the fairly wealthy industrial region of Silesia in southern Poland where his own constituency is.
"Deputies are attacked (by their constituents) because Silesia is not being dealt with fairly but is treated like a cow to be milked," PAP quoted Pistelok as saying.

Italy's Northern League, which sponsored the referendum, said on Monday that 99.7 percent of the some six million voters taking part had favoured seceding from Italy and creating their own independent northern state to be called Padania.
The referendum, seen by Italian mainstream parties and abroad as little more than a political demonstration, has no legal value.
"The Italian authorities have not approached us on deputy Pistelok's involvement in the referendum," PAP quoted Foreign Ministry spokesman Boguslaw Majewski as saying.
"The Foreign Ministry would like to know about such trips and usually we are informed, but this time that did not happen," he added.

A parliamentary official told PAP Pistelok went to Italy on a private visit without consulting anyone, while a spokesman for the PSL's parliamentary club also said nobody there had known anything of Pistelok's travel plans.
Besides Pistelok, the North Italy plebiscite was attended by one senator from Croatia as well as several MPs from Catalonia and Uruguay, PAP added.
